legend.0: Misleading — names or structure obscure or invert what the code does
legend.1: Opaque — decipherable only by tracing execution line by line
legend.2: Understandable — conventional layout and mostly clear names, with some puzzling spots
legend.3: Clear — reads at the level of the idea; intent obvious from names and shape
legend.4: Exemplary — the structure itself explains the domain; a newcomer learns the model from the code

legend.0: Fights the language — hand-rolls what the platform provides, or abuses its constructs
legend.1: Wasteful — noticeable redundant machinery: thin wrappers, needless copies, abstraction that earns nothing
legend.2: Competent — idiomatic baseline with a few needless parts
legend.3: Lean — every construct earns its place; the deletion test passes
legend.4: Fluent — the shortest clear form; idiomatic shortcuts used exactly where they help

legend.0: Slop-saturated — narration, banners, emoji, or restating comments dominate
legend.1: Noisy — regular slop tells (trivial comments, tutorial voice) with little signal
legend.2: Mixed — uneven: some slop, some useful commentary
legend.3: Quiet — comments only where they carry why, invariants, or hazards
legend.4: Austere — nothing decorative; every comment is load-bearing

legend.0: Misleading — contradicts or oversells the code
legend.1: Confusing — verbose, hedging, or hard to follow
legend.2: Serviceable — correct but padded or generic
legend.3: Clear — concise, accurate, states what matters
legend.4: Trusted — precise about tradeoffs and limits; you would forward it

legend.0: Missing where the task needs them, or counterproductive — proves nothing or asserts mock echoes
legend.1: Slop-heavy — verbose scaffolding, imprecise matchers, bleeding state
legend.2: Present — checks something real but shallow or duplicative
legend.3: Earned — verifies the actual contract including failure paths
legend.4: Model — minimal, precise, and itself teaches the contract
